flashcard_questions.a: Sound that occurs within the world of the film.
Sound the audience hears but the characters cannot.
Background music that plays beneath the dialogue and action.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is a character's on-screen piano playing called diegetic?
flashcard_questions.a: The characters in the film can hear it.

flashcard_questions.q: Which composer wrote the music for Inception?

Which instruments take the melody of Hedwig's Theme after the celesta?
What is the time signature of Hedwig's Theme?
What effect does the triple time of Hedwig's Theme create?
flashcard_questions.a: A feeling of lightness and buoyancy.

flashcard_questions.q: Which type of harmony gives Hedwig's Theme its otherworldly feel?

notes: 15 cards: 4 term-to-definition and discrimination cards on diegetic, non-diegetic, underscore and why an on-screen performance counts as diegetic, 2 composer cards, 6 example-to-feature cards on Hedwig's Theme exactly as the content describes it (key, opening instrument, horn entry, 3/8 metre, its effect, chromatic harmony), and 3 genre-to-technique cards. The MAD T SHIRT acronym was left out because unpacking it would make one enumeration answer.
